1.note: Literally "before their encamping". חנה is "to encamp, to come to rest"; the word is chosen for the rhyme with הֱיוֹתָם. Read as "before they have settled", that is, before they happen. Uncertain.

2.he: וּבְיָדָיו כְּלִי נְחשֶׁת. וְעָלָיו מַעֲשֵׂי רֶשֶׁת
2.note: An astrolabe: a bronze disc with an open-work "net" (the rete) that carries the star pointers. The phrase is that of the bronze grating of the altar, Exod 27:4.

3.note: Probably the technical terms for a planet's "fall" (dejection) and "exaltation", the signs where its power is weakest and strongest; also simply its setting and rising.

4.note: Gen 25:16 says this of the twelve princes of Ishmael, "by their courts and their castles". Here it is the twelve signs of the zodiac, with the astrological "houses" as their courts and castles.

5.note: תולדות is "generations, offspring". The moon was held to rule birth and growth; "its phases" is also possible.

6.note: הצומח, "the one that sprouts", is the Hebrew astrological term for the ascendant (the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a given moment).

7.note: יתדות, "pegs", is the Hebrew term (as in Abraham Ibn Ezra) for the four cardinal points of a horoscope: ascendant, midheaven, descendant and lowest point. "Chords" (literally "cords, strings") are probably the lines that join them in the chart. The "four feet" are those of the Ark, Exod 25:12.

8.note: The twelve signs follow in order, each with a pun or a verse: Ram (Aries), Bull (Taurus), Twins (Gemini), Crab (Cancer), Lion (Leo), Virgin (Virgo), Scales (Libra), Scorpion (Scorpio), the one who handles the bow (Sagittarius), Kid or Goat (Capricorn), Bucket (Aquarius), Fishes (Pisces).

9.note: Play on בְּתוּלָה (Virgin, Virgo) and בְּעוּלָה (a married woman, one who is no longer a virgin): even the Virgin is his.

10.note: מזל גדי, "the sign of the kid", is Capricorn. Samson tore the lion "as one tears a kid" (Judg 14:6); here the kid itself is torn. In the next lines דְּלִי, "bucket" (Aquarius), meets "a drop from a bucket" (Isa 40:15).

11.he: יָשִׂים אִישׁ מִכֶּם יָדוֹ על הַחוֹל
11.note: Geomancy (Arabic ʿilm al-raml, "the science of the sand"): the diviner makes rows of dots in sand or dust, reduces them to figures, and reads them, here together with the astrolabe and the horoscope.

12.he: כִּי בוֹ יִוָּדַע הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִן הַחֹל
12.note: Pun: חוֹל "sand" and חֹל "profane" sound the same. "By the sand the holy is known from the profane"; the pun comes back in the astrologer's oath.

13.note: עֶרֶץ (literally "might") is a poetic name for the heavens, as the note in the Project Ben-Yehuda text explains.

14.note: Ishmaelites are Muslims; the uncircumcised are Christians. So the visitors can only be Jews.

15.he: וְעַל שֶׁה פְזוּרָה הֲתִמָּלֵט מִשִּׁנֵי אֲרָיוֹת
15.note: Jer 50:17: "Israel is a scattered sheep; lions have driven it away". The edition points מִשִּׁנֵי, "from the teeth of". The same letters can be read מִשְּׁנֵי, "from two lions", that is, Islam and Christendom, which the astrologer has just named.

16.note: Literally "except with our breath between our teeth": barely alive. Compare Job 13:14, "I take my flesh in my teeth".
